title: Boléro · Ravel (synthesized arrangement)

arrangement.scope: Four-bar introduction; complete opening flute theme from original bars 5–21, including ties and rests; short pizzicato/snare turnaround.
arrangement.instruments: Procedurally synthesized flute, reduced C/G pizzicato cello/viola accompaniment, and the signature two-bar snare pattern.
arrangement.changes: Reduced instrumentation, synthesized timbres, restrained dynamics and a loop turnaround. This is an excerpt arrangement, not the complete orchestration or a historical performance.
arrangement.audio_source: All PCM is synthesized locally by arcade-music.js; no third-party recording or instrumental sample is used.

sources.title: Nicolas Sceaux: Ravel_Bolero — composer score transcription
sources.license: CC0 1.0 Universal, as declared by the repository LICENSE and the rendered flute part footer.
sources.use: Pitch, duration, tie and snare-pattern transcription, plus the opening accompaniment reduction.

sources.title: Boléro — Flûte 1, Éditions Nicolas Sceaux, 2016
sources.use: Rendered score visually checked against the source notation; footer declares CC0 1.0.

sources.title: IMSLP: Boléro, M.81 — original edition bibliography
sources.locator: First-edition parts: Paris, Durand & Cie., 1929, plate D. & F. 11.780; flute #299525 and snare #299518
sources.use: Historical publication and public-domain catalogue provenance. The historical scan was not used as the transcription master.

verification: Pure regression checks the opening pitches and cadence, ties across barlines, full three-quarter bar durations, alternating 10/14-attack snare cycles, actual PCM fundamentals, finite headroom and the unchanged playback lifecycle.
limits: No claim of orchestral realism or full-work coverage; speaker output and perceived recognizability require listening.
